reason: French 'pelliculaire' (exocarp, rhytidome) = forming a thin skin-like film; FLOPO:0991046 membranous is thin, flexible and membrane-like. For bark, 'rhytidome pelliculaire' is thin papery outer bark.
'sub-' + lignified = somewhat woody: the approximate-value qualifier on PATO_0002348 ligneous, as for 'suborbicular'.
'Radicante aux noeuds/à la base' = the stem roots at the nodes, i.e. bears adventitious roots (EXACT synonym in PO_0000042). The place (nodes, base) is the part of the stem.
French 'cannelé' = fluted, which the previous review mapped to PATO_0001948 furrowed (RELATED synonym fluted).
French 'nervuré' = veined/nerved; same rule as 'veined' and 'nerved' in the previous review. Direction (longitudinal, transverse) is a further quality of the veins.

target: new: compound of two values (elliptic PATO_0000947 of the bearer + acuminate PATO_0002228 of its apex)
reason: Two values that inhere in different parts: the outline is elliptic and the apex is acuminate. No single class is needed.
Negation of FLOPO:0991107 peltate. For 'non-peltate scales', the bearer is the scale of the organ named.
OCR error for 'plano-convex' (l read as i); FLOPO:0991184 exists.
Latin 'hirtus' = hairy with stiffish hairs, the usual equivalent of hirsute (not the diminutive hirtellous).

target: new: compound of two values (puberulous FLOPO:0991049 + ash-grey colour of the hairs)
reason: Puberulent with ash-grey hairs: an indumentum value plus the colour of the hairs, not one quality. 'puberulcnt' is an OCR variant.

Two unrelated senses. 'Racemes interlocked back to back' is a relation needing its second term (PATO_0002437 interlocked with is relational). 'Interlocked grain' is a wood-anatomy fibre orientation that is too rare here to justify a class.
An apex ending abruptly in a short, stiff, sharp point is what FLOPO:0991054 mucronate defines; 'pungent' only stresses the sharpness.
A grass ligule 'a fringe of hairs' is a ligule consisting of a fringe of short hairs; PATO_0040008 fringed is an edge shape with threads along the border.
The floret lacks a (functional) palea. 'Significant' admits a vestige, which the absence rule does not capture.
Seed-coat or cortical cells that are brick-shaped (in section) are rectangular. The bearer is the cell (seed coat epidermis cells), not the seed.
For leaves and leaflets, 'pungent' means ending in a sharp, piercing point, so this negates PATO_0001419 sharp. It is not the odour sense.

target: new: compound of two values (spotted PATO_0000333 + red PATO_0000322 of the flecks)
reason: A marking pattern plus the colour of the marks; both values exist and the compound needs no class.
In PO, caudex is a synonym of stem, so a 'caudex-like stem' carries no class distinction. The meaning (a short, thickened, perennial stem base) would have to be stated through those qualities.
A likeness to another part, with no stated quality and few statements. Where the bracts actually form an involucre, the bearer is involucre (PO_0009100).

label: ternately decompound
definition: A structural quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of its being divided into three parts more than once, each primary division being itself ternately divided.
reason: A standard leaf-division character with no PATO or FLOPO term. It is the ternate counterpart of FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate and sits beside FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate (parent PATO:0000141). 'Ternately and pinnately decompound' is two values (pattern 07).

target: new: compound of two values (ciliate margin + arachnoid (cobwebby) hairs)
reason: Margins fringed with cilia that are long, fine and tangled: a margin value plus a hair quality, not one quality. 'Arachnoid' itself has no term yet.
A seed surface covered with small rounded smooth bumps, like pebbles, is a surface with small rounded protuberances (FLOPO:0991060). 'Minutely pebbly' fits verruculose FLOPO:0991088 nearly as well.

target: new: compound of two values (scabrous FLOPO:0991058 + ciliolate margin/keel)
reason: Keels or margins with minute cilia that make them rough: two values (scabrous, ciliolate) on one bearer.
'Collapsing on drying' = caving in, PATO_0001478 collapsed; 'on drying' goes to the specimen-condition pattern (docs/odp/06-specimen-condition.md).
Bearing cystoliths (cells with calcium carbonate concretions), which are a kind of idioblast. PO has no cystolith/lithocyst class, so a PO term request would make this precise.
PATO_0000947 elliptic has the synonym ellipsoid; 'broadly' (a lower length:width ratio) is a refinement that does not change the class.
A doubly serrulate margin is serrulate, with the larger teeth themselves serrulate. Mapping to FLOPO:0991081 is correct but loses the doubling, which is too rare for a class.
Ocreae and bracts 'tattering at apices' become irregularly torn, which is FLOPO:0991115 lacerate. The apex is the part of the bearer.
Leaves appearing at the same time as the flowers (or the reverse): a temporal relation between two parts, like hysteranthous. PATO_0000695 synchronous concerns processes.
A margin with deep, sharp, forward-pointing teeth is serrate; 'incised' only stresses the depth. Mapping to PATO_0001206 is correct, as with doubly serrulate.
